project.name: DISARM Explorer
project.canonical_source: content-addressed static checkout; VCS revision is unavailable in this checkout

owner.escalation: Qdev Platform owner for manifest, catalog and shared-capability registration

platform_manifest.meaning: This boundary contract supplies product-local evidence to the root manifest. The Platform registry remains the bilateral acceptance authority.

capabilities.rationale: The product is a static read-only explorer and ships no QazStack primitive, session, queue, service or backend runtime.
capabilities.boundary: A future server-side workflow, account, mutation or shared primitive requires a QazStack consumer contract before implementation.

The local candidate uses AVDS 4.7.0 with adapter 1.3.5. Runtime proof is release-specific: every changed candidate requires separately authorized promotion plus check_runtime_evidence.py, smoke_live.sh and public browser evidence before parity is claimed.
capabilities.review_by: at every AVDS or release change

capabilities.rationale: No collection, queue, ingestion service or QazPipe endpoint is used; the verified DISARM matrix is committed as a static public projection.
capabilities.boundary: Any automated source intake must declare provenance, failure semantics and a QazPipe contract before use.

capabilities.rationale: The browser reads only data/disarm.json and makes no QazLake query.
capabilities.boundary: A QazLake-backed projection needs freshness, access, retention and degraded-mode evidence before publication.

capabilities.rationale: There is no compute job, model invocation or server-side execution in this static product.
capabilities.boundary: Any permitted compute workload must declare its interface, non-mutation rule, timeout and fallback.

capabilities.rationale: The incident view uses disclosed local country reference points and a list alternative; it does not call a QazGeo API or dataset.
capabilities.boundary: A geographic service integration must document its dataset, precision and fallback before use.
capabilities.review_by: before replacing the local reference-point layer

capabilities.rationale: The deployed entrypoint is protected by a server-side PIN session boundary. The static source has no user accounts, roles, mutations or identity SDK.
capabilities.boundary: This is not evidence of Platform Identity/OIDC adoption. Any account, role or mutation flow requires a manifest and an identity integration contract.
capabilities.review_by: before changing the authentication or mutation boundary

data_and_privacy.classification: public framework data and public documentation metadata only
data_and_privacy.processing_boundary: All product data is loaded in the browser from static files. Browser preferences, annotations and selected playbook items stay in browser localStorage and are not uploaded by this product.
data_and_privacy.private_data: No credentials, personal data, private endpoints or protected source text are included in the static data contract.
data_and_privacy.retention: The product has no server-side application database; local browser storage is controlled by the user agent.
data_and_privacy.degraded_state: The interface exposes loading, stale, degraded, offline and error states when the static data fetch cannot complete.

routes_and_delivery.route_ledger: seven tab panels: overview, red, blue, search, incidents, playbook and about
routes_and_delivery.runtime_boundary: The unauthenticated root is expected to redirect to /login; explicitly allowlisted public contracts remain readable. The edge serves those contracts locally and proxies the protected document root to the serving origin, so both hosts must be aligned. A release is not proven without fresh source-to-runtime identity parity. check_runtime_evidence.py must pass before live smoke can be treated as release proof.
routes_and_delivery.rollback_boundary: The deployment procedure requires a timestamped snapshot before public files are changed.
